You are doing OPS/INFRASTRUCTURE hardening for Nxeon, a production VPS hosting platform on a Proxmox VE 9 server (Debian 13, public IP 51.79.162.96). Read /opt/nxeon/CLAUDE.md first for architecture and safety rules. Production app is at /opt/nxeon (services nxeon-web/nxeon-worker, nginx :80, Postgres DB "nxeon"); staging at /opt/nxeon-staging (DB "nxeon_staging", :8080).

STRICT SCOPE — you may ONLY create/modify:
- Files under /opt/nxeon/scripts/**
- systemd units under /etc/systemd/system/nxeon-*.{service,timer}
- nginx config /etc/nginx/sites-available/nxeon and /etc/nginx/sites-available/nxeon-staging
- /etc/nxeon/** (create for config if needed)
Do NOT touch: any /opt/nxeon/app, /opt/nxeon/lib, /opt/nxeon/worker, /opt/nxeon/prisma, /opt/nxeon/components, package.json, or .env files. Do NOT run git commit (the orchestrator commits). Do NOT restart nxeon-web/nxeon-worker. You MAY reload nginx (nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx) and create/enable your own new timers.

CRITICAL SAFETY: This is a LIVE production host reachable only via SSH on port 22. NEVER configure a firewall that could drop port 22 — if you set up nftables/iptables filtering at all, port 22 (SSH), 80, 443, 8080, 8006 (Proxmox), and the VPS NAT ranges (20000-29999, 30000-30999) MUST stay open, and you must NOT flush the existing NXEON_FWD / NXEON_FWD_STG NAT chains or the MASQUERADE rule. Given the risk, DO NOT implement host firewalling in this task — leave it for a human-reviewed change; note it in the report instead.

TASKS (do all, test each):

1. **Database backups** — script /opt/nxeon/scripts/backup-db.sh that pg_dumps BOTH databases (nxeon, nxeon_staging) as the postgres user to /tank/backup/db/ with timestamped filenames (gzip), and prunes dumps older than 14 days. Create systemd service+timer nxeon-backup-db.{service,timer} running daily ~03:15. Enable the timer. TEST by running the script once and confirming a dump file appears and restores-list works (gunzip -t).

2. **VM backups** — script /opt/nxeon/scripts/backup-vms.sh that runs `vzdump` for all customer VMs (running/stopped QEMU guests with VMID >= 100 and < 9000, i.e. exclude templates 9000-9999) to storage "backup" (compress zstd, mode snapshot), pruning to keep last 3 per VM (vzdump --prune-backups keep-last=3, storage-level). Create nxeon-backup-vms.{service,timer} weekly ~Sunday 04:30. Enable. TEST the script's VM-selection logic with a dry echo (don't necessarily run a full vzdump if no eligible VMs exist — but if a customer VM exists, running it is fine; otherwise log "no eligible VMs").

3. **HTTPS with self-signed cert** — generate a self-signed cert (/etc/nxeon/tls/ , 2048-bit, CN=51.79.162.96, 3650 days) and add TLS to nginx: production listens 443 (self-signed) alongside 80, staging listens 8443 alongside 8080. Keep 80/8080 working (do NOT force-redirect yet — a real Let's Encrypt cert needs a domain first; note that). Proxy config identical to the existing :80/:8080 blocks. nginx -t and reload. TEST with curl -k https://127.0.0.1/ and curl -k https://127.0.0.1:8443/ returning 200. Add a note that COOKIE_SECURE should be enabled in .env only once a trusted (LE) cert is installed.

4. **Additional OS templates** — download cloud images and create Proxmox templates, then register them so the platform offers them:
   - AlmaLinux 9 (https://repo.almalinux.org/almalinux/9/cloud/x86_64/images/AlmaLinux-9-GenericCloud-latest.x86_64.qcow2) as VMID 9002
   - Rocky Linux 9 (https://download.rockylinux.org/pub/rocky/9/images/x86_64/Rocky-9-GenericCloud-Base.latest.x86_64.qcow2) as VMID 9003
   - Ubuntu 22.04 (https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/jammy/current/jammy-server-cloudimg-amd64.img) as VMID 9004
   Mirror EXACTLY how templates 9000/9001 were built (study `qm config 9000` first: scsi0 on vmdata with import-from, ide2 cloudinit, vmbr1 net, agent, serial0/vga serial0, cicustom vendor=backup:snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml, then `qm template`). Download to /var/lib/vz/template/cloudimg/. After each template is built, register it in the DB via psql as the postgres user:
     `sudo -u postgres psql -d nxeon -c "INSERT INTO \"OsTemplate\" (id,slug,name,vmid,active) VALUES (gen_random_cuid-ish...)"` — BUT Prisma cuid isn't available in SQL. Instead use: `INSERT INTO \"OsTemplate\" (id,slug,name,vmid,active) VALUES (md5(random()::text), 'almalinux-9','AlmaLinux 9',9002,true) ON CONFLICT (slug) DO UPDATE SET vmid=excluded.vmid,active=true;` (a random md5 hex id is a valid unique string id). Do the same for the nxeon_staging DB. TEST: `qm list` shows 9002/9003/9004 as templates and psql shows the OsTemplate rows.

Work carefully and idempotently (scripts re-runnable). Report: what you built, test results for each, and the firewall item you deliberately deferred. If a cloud image download fails, note it and continue with the others.

1	# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform
2	
3	Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
8	- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
9	- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
10	- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
11	- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
12	- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).
13	
14	## Portals & design system
15	
16	- Customer portal (`app/dashboard/**`) and admin ops portal (`app/admin/**`) are separate sidebar apps sharing `components/portal/Shell.tsx` (sidebar, topbar, notifications bell, ⌘K command palette backed by `/api/search`).
17	- Design system lives in `app/globals.css` (glass cards, gradient buttons, navy palette) + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` + `components/ui/charts.tsx` (dependency-free SVG charts). Use these — do not add chart libraries.
18	- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
19	- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners).
20	
21	## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)
22	
23	- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id).
24	- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
25	- **GitHub**: `.git/hooks/post-commit` auto-pushes when an `origin` remote exists; configure once with `scripts/setup-github.sh <remote-url>`.
26	
27	## Conventions
28	
29	- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
30	- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
31	- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
32	- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
33	- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
34	
35	## Commands
36	
37	- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
38	- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker`
39	- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
40	- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
41	- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`
42	
43	## Environments
44	
45	- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
46	- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080. Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
47	- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
48	- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at :8080 → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. The improvement agent should test changes on staging before promoting.
49	
50	## Safety rules
51	
52	- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
53	- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
54	- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
55	- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
56	- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
57	- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

#!/bin/bash
# Nxeon — PostgreSQL logical backups
# pg_dumps both databases (nxeon, nxeon_staging) as the postgres user to
# /tank/backup/db/, gzip-compressed with timestamped filenames, and prunes
# dumps older than RETENTION_DAYS. Idempotent / re-runnable.
set -euo pipefail

BACKUP_DIR="/tank/backup/db"
RETENTION_DAYS="${NXEON_DB_RETENTION_DAYS:-14}"
DATABASES=(nxeon nxeon_staging)
TS="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"

mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"

log() { echo "[$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z)] $*"; }

rc=0
for db in "${DATABASES[@]}"; do
    # Skip cleanly if the database does not exist (e.g. staging removed).
    if ! sudo -u postgres psql -tAc "SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname='${db}'" | grep -q 1; then
        log "database '${db}' not present, skipping"
        continue
    fi

    dest="${BACKUP_DIR}/${db}-${TS}.sql.gz"
    tmp="${dest}.partial"
    log "dumping '${db}' -> ${dest}"
    if sudo -u postgres pg_dump --no-owner --no-privileges "$db" | gzip -c > "$tmp"; then
        mv "$tmp" "$dest"
        # Integrity check: gzip stream must decompress cleanly.
        if gunzip -t "$dest"; then
            log "OK ${dest} ($(du -h "$dest" | cut -f1))"
        else
            log "ERROR gunzip -t failed for ${dest}"
            rc=1
        fi
    else
        log "ERROR pg_dump failed for '${db}'"
        rm -f "$tmp"
        rc=1
    fi
done

# Prune dumps older than RETENTION_DAYS.
log "pruning dumps older than ${RETENTION_DAYS} days in ${BACKUP_DIR}"
find "$BACKUP_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.sql.gz' -mtime "+${RETENTION_DAYS}" -print -delete || true

log "done (exit ${rc})"
exit "$rc"

#!/bin/bash
# Nxeon — customer VM backups via vzdump
# Backs up all QEMU guests (running or stopped) with VMID in [100, 9000)
# to Proxmox storage "backup" using zstd compression, snapshot mode, keeping
# the last 3 backups per VM at the storage level. Templates (9000-9999) are
# excluded. Idempotent / re-runnable.
set -euo pipefail

STORAGE="${NXEON_VM_BACKUP_STORAGE:-backup}"
KEEP_LAST="${NXEON_VM_BACKUP_KEEP:-3}"

log() { echo "[$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z)] $*"; }

# Collect eligible VMIDs: numeric first column of `qm list`, VMID>=100, <9000.
mapfile -t VMIDS < <(qm list 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR>1 && $1 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ && $1>=100 && $1<9000 {print $1}' | sort -n)

if [ "${#VMIDS[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    log "no eligible VMs (none with 100 <= VMID < 9000); nothing to back up"
    exit 0
fi

log "eligible customer VMs: ${VMIDS[*]}"

# Optional dry-run: NXEON_VM_BACKUP_DRYRUN=1 only prints the selection/command.
if [ "${NXEON_VM_BACKUP_DRYRUN:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    log "DRY RUN — would run: vzdump ${VMIDS[*]} --storage ${STORAGE} --compress zstd --mode snapshot --prune-backups keep-last=${KEEP_LAST}"
    exit 0
fi

log "running vzdump -> storage '${STORAGE}' (zstd, snapshot, keep-last=${KEEP_LAST})"
vzdump "${VMIDS[@]}" \
    --storage "$STORAGE" \
    --compress zstd \
    --mode snapshot \
    --prune-backups "keep-last=${KEEP_LAST}"

log "done"

#!/bin/bash
# Nxeon — build additional Proxmox cloud-init templates
# Mirrors exactly how templates 9000/9001 were built:
#   scsi0 on vmdata via import-from, ide2 cloudinit, vmbr1 net, agent enabled,
#   serial0 socket + vga serial0, cicustom vendor snippet, then `qm template`.
# Downloads cloud images to /var/lib/vz/template/cloudimg/ and registers each
# template in the OsTemplate table of both the nxeon and nxeon_staging DBs.
# Idempotent: skips builds where the VMID already exists; DB upserts on slug.
set -euo pipefail

IMGDIR="/var/lib/vz/template/cloudimg"
STORAGE="vmdata"
VENDOR="backup:snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml"
DBS=(nxeon nxeon_staging)

mkdir -p "$IMGDIR"
log() { echo "[$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z)] $*"; }

# template spec: VMID | slug | display name | filename | url
TEMPLATES=(
  "9002|almalinux-9|AlmaLinux 9|AlmaLinux-9-GenericCloud-latest.x86_64.qcow2|https://repo.almalinux.org/almalinux/9/cloud/x86_64/images/AlmaLinux-9-GenericCloud-latest.x86_64.qcow2"
  "9003|rocky-9|Rocky Linux 9|Rocky-9-GenericCloud-Base.latest.x86_64.qcow2|https://download.rockylinux.org/pub/rocky/9/images/x86_64/Rocky-9-GenericCloud-Base.latest.x86_64.qcow2"
  "9004|ubuntu-22-04|Ubuntu 22.04 LTS|jammy-server-cloudimg-amd64.img|https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/jammy/current/jammy-server-cloudimg-amd64.img"
)

register_db() {
    local slug="$1" name="$2" vmid="$3"
    for db in "${DBS[@]}"; do
        sudo -u postgres psql -d "$db" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c \
"INSERT INTO \"OsTemplate\" (id,slug,name,vmid,active)
 VALUES (md5(random()::text || clock_timestamp()::text), '${slug}', '${name}', ${vmid}, true)
 ON CONFLICT (slug) DO UPDATE SET vmid=excluded.vmid, name=excluded.name, active=true;" \
        && log "registered '${slug}' (vmid ${vmid}) in DB '${db}'"
    done
}

build_one() {
    local vmid="$1" slug="$2" name="$3" fname="$4" url="$5"
    local img="${IMGDIR}/${fname}"

    if qm status "$vmid" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        log "VMID ${vmid} (${slug}) already exists — skipping build, re-registering DB"
        register_db "$slug" "$name" "$vmid"
        return 0
    fi

    log "downloading ${name} image"
    if ! wget -q --show-progress -O "${img}.partial" "$url"; then
        log "ERROR: download failed for ${name} (${url}) — skipping"
        rm -f "${img}.partial"
        return 1
    fi
    mv "${img}.partial" "$img"

    log "creating VM ${vmid} (${name})"
    qm create "$vmid" \
        --name "tpl-${slug}" \
        --memory 1024 \
        --cores 1 \
        --cpu host \
        --net0 "virtio,bridge=vmbr1" \
        --scsihw virtio-scsi-single \
        --ostype l26 \
        --agent enabled=1 \
        --serial0 socket \
        --vga serial0

    log "importing disk to ${STORAGE}"
    qm set "$vmid" --scsi0 "${STORAGE}:0,import-from=${img},discard=on"
    qm set "$vmid" --ide2 "${STORAGE}:cloudinit,media=cdrom"
    qm set "$vmid" --boot order=scsi0
    qm set "$vmid" --cicustom "vendor=${VENDOR}"

    log "converting VMID ${vmid} to template"
    qm template "$vmid"

    register_db "$slug" "$name" "$vmid"
    log "template ${name} (VMID ${vmid}) built"
}

rc=0
for spec in "${TEMPLATES[@]}"; do
    IFS='|' read -r vmid slug name fname url <<<"$spec"
    build_one "$vmid" "$slug" "$name" "$fname" "$url" || rc=1
done
exit "$rc"
